replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
Ok so first -- I agree that the voxelized environment in the splash is superior to minecraft style environments in game. It's certainly a lot harder to pull off, because it requires a lot more from the engine with a full voxelized setup... But it's theoretically doable and if done well could bring the game up several notches in the end.

However, I vehemently disagree on the mixed style being "inconsistent and amateur". Yes, it is inferior (imo), however have you not heard of Trove? A very successful game that used that exact mixed style with voxelized character designs and full block environments. Or Veloren, or PixArk, or Earth Defense Force: World Brothers. There is very clearly at least some market of players who would not be turned off by the style, and it is a proven option, especially considering that the workload in implementation is much lighter than the full voxelized environment. 

That being said, trying to compete in the Minecraft space is incredibly difficult since most people who love the style will just play Minecraft instead (mods mean there are so many different ways to play that you really have to make extreme improvements in areas just to stand out.) Despite it being much harder to implement full voxel, it may be easier than trying to win over people through other means. Something OP should maybe consider, at least long term, because it's true that the space is rather congested. If a full voxel environment is too daunting, they may also want to consider looking to something like Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 1/2 which utilizes the simpler full block shapes for environment, but pulls on high quality stylized textures to break free from the minecraft comparisons (also it's futuristic so it would likely not be competing).
